summary_html: Case dismissed due to **unsubstantiated evidence** or court determination that allegations not proven. Federal oversight requires accurate recording of such closures for audit and funding compliance.

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Jennifer M.
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the finding of abuse and neglect and the order placing the mother on the Central Registry, holding she could not be found to have abused an unborn child by conduct occurring while she neither knew nor had reason to know she was pregnant, and that the drug-test evidence was inadmissible hearsay without foundation.
key_cases.relevance: This is a model of a case reversed and effectively closed for failure of proof.
key_cases.quote: the family court erred in finding Mother abused and neglected her unborn Child based upon conduct occurring while Mother did not know or have reason to know she was pregnant

key_cases.case_name: South Carolina Department of Social Services v. Gamble
key_cases.court: Court of Appeals of South Carolina
key_cases.holding: The court reversed dismissal of a removal case, holding the statute requires that the merits hearing be scheduled to be held — not necessarily completed — within thirty-five days of the removal petition, and rejecting the parent's constitutional challenge.
key_cases.relevance: The decision limits dismissal as a remedy for timeline violations in removal cases.
key_cases.quote: The statute requires the family court to schedule a hearing on the merits to be held within thirty-five days of the removal petition.

key_cases.case_name: Beattie v. Aiken County Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that parents whose case was closed as unfounded may not examine the DSS case file, that 'report' covers all investigative information and the reporter's identity is never disclosable, and that FOIA requires separation and release of non-exempt material where a court is asked to conduct that review.
key_cases.relevance: Beattie governs the records consequences of a case closed without a founded finding.
key_cases.quote: The clear language of § 20-7-650 prohibits the disclosure of the DSS case file to Appellants or to anyone else.

key_cases.holding: The court clarified the family court standard of review, holding that while appellate courts review de novo and may find facts by their own view of the preponderance of the evidence, the appellant still bears the burden of showing error and the family court's credibility findings are respected.
key_cases.relevance: Lewis fixes the standard an appellate court applies when reviewing a dismissal or a finding that allegations were not proven.
key_cases.quote: consistent with our constitutional authority for de novo review, an appellant is not relieved of his burden to demonstrate error in the family court's findings of fact

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Fourth Circuit reversed, holding that the confidential retention of records of a child abuse investigation classified 'unsubstantiated' and 'ruled out' violates neither substantive nor procedural due process, so the state officials were entitled to qualified immunity.
key_cases.relevance: Where a case closes without a founded finding, Hodge is the controlling circuit authority that the investigative record may still lawfully be retained and indexed.
key_cases.quote: The record before us presents no substantive due process violation of a familial privacy liberty interest by virtue of the retention of the Hodge investigation report
